Hi Rachel / Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a small on-prem pilot at three remote locations (single-rack, 2U servers per site). Before we book the on-site resources, could you confirm the minimum cluster layout and persistent storage approach you recommend for running a compact Redwood Private deployment?

Constraints to call out:
- Each site: 3 x 2U nodes (one is beefy for inference, two for control + mgmt workloads).
- Limited bandwidth, egress strictly controlled via a firewall appliance; some nights will be effectively air-gapped for backups.
- No central SAN available; we can add a NAS device or attach NVMe per server.
- Need to support a small GPU for low-latency inference and local caching for model weights.
- Strong compliance need: encrypted at-rest, and a minimal audit trail for model versioning.

I've attached an inventory spreadsheet with power, NICs, and rack constraints. Can we get a short checklist of the cluster requirements (node types, storage classes, backup strategy) and any guardrails we should enforce on the site ops side?

Best,
Maria Ortega
Head of Site Ops — GreenTech Industries

Hi Maria — thanks, this is clear and the inventory helps. High-level recommendation (TL;DR below, full checklist attached):

TL;DR recommendations:
- 3-node cluster per site: 1 inference node (GPU, NVMe local cache), 1 control/infra node (etcd + master-like services), 1 shared-worker for non-latency workloads and backups.
- Two storage classes: local-fast (hostPath/CSI on NVMe) for model cache and emptyDir workload scratch; network-backed PV (NFS or S3-compatible over a private link) for stateful data + snapshots.
- Use Velero with an S3-compatible object store reachable during maintenance windows; encrypt object store with customer KMS.
- Strict egress whitelist and an intermittent pull-proxy for image/model updates.

Detailed checklist (summary):
- Node sizing: inference node: 2 x 16 cores, 256 GB RAM, 1 x A40/RTX6000-class GPU (or similar), 2 x 2 TB NVMe in RAID1 for cache and model volumes.
- Control node: 16 cores, 64 GB RAM, 1 x 1 TB NVMe, run etcd (3-node etcd cluster is ideal across sites but for the pilot we'll colocate etcd on control nodes and enable local backups).
- Worker node: 8 cores, 32 GB RAM, standard SSDs for logs and non-critical workloads.
- Networking: dedicate a management NIC for control plane traffic; data-plane NIC isolated. Host firewall should allow only egress to: our patch/proxy endpoint, S3 endpoint (for backups) and telemetry endpoints (list provided).
- Storage classes: local-ssd-fast (CSI driver to expose NVMe), network-pv (NFS v4.1 or MinIO S3 gateway).
- Kubelet evictions: set high_memory_pressure (avoid pod OOMs), enable local-storage eviction thresholds (<10% left triggers eviction).
- Model caching: use hostPath-backed persistentVolumeClaims for weights with a small sidecar that reconciles model versions from the model registry during maintenance windows.
- Secrets and KMS: store secrets in sealed vault or KMS-protected store; recommend using customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption.
- Backups: Velero scheduled nightly during maintenance window; if site is air-gapped nightly, run local snapshot + ship when link available.
- Audit: enable kube-audit and forward compressed daily bundles to S3 for retention.

I'll attach a one-page plan (proposed-node-matrix.pdf) and a short runbook for the pilot. Can we set a 30–45 minute call early next week to walk through specifics and confirm which NICs and firewall rules they can open?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim

Folks — quick technical notes and a couple of caveats based on the constraints: 

1) etcd: running etcd local to each site is ok for this pilot, but we must ensure consistent snapshot and restore docs. I'll add a step to automatically validate WAL integrity after each snapshot and ship to object storage when reachable.

2) NVMe endurance: using NVMe for model cache is fine; put a thin write-through caching layer (cachefs or use container-local caching) and make the model cache recreateable from the registry so we don't rely on long retention.

3) PV selection: prefer CSI drivers (local-csi) over plain hostPath for lifecycle consistency. If the site ops cannot install CSI, we'll fall back to carefully curated hostPath with systemd service to label disks.

4) Network: implement a pull-proxy (air-gapped friendly) that mirrors container images and model artifacts on a schedule. This avoids opening broad egress during normal operation.

5) Monitoring/health: keep a small Prometheus + pushgateway in the control node; configure alerts for disk pressure, NIC errors, and GPU temperature. We can reduce cardinality to control storage.

I'll update the internal repo with a starter Helm chart and a sample Velero schedule for "delta-only" uploads which should minimize bandwidth during limited windows.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Platform Engineer — Redwood Inference
